waivers.reason: Not reachable from stdin. main() reads stdin ONLY to derive session_id for logging (line 178); the branch taken is decided by throttled(), which reads .claude/hooks/_state/repo-sync-cadence.json, and by build_message(), which shells out to git log and git rev-list inside two clone paths hardcoded off __file__ (Projects/Agent-Governance-Research/framework-repo and /repo). No stdin field can change either, and the hook exposes no env override for the state file or the repo paths, unlike memory-context-guard.py. This is NOT a 'could not work out the input' waiver and I did not tune the expectation down to silent: I loaded the module and called build_message() against synthetic REPOS, which produced '[REPO-SYNC: CLONE UNREADABLE] AGF (agent-governance-framework)...' for a directory with no .git, and '[REPO-SYNC CADENCE: OVERDUE] AGR last commit 234d ago (cadence 14d)...' for a real temp git repo committed with GIT_COMMITTER_DATE=2026-01-01. The detector genuinely fires; its trip is simply unprobeable by the stdin method this suite uses. Against live state it is currently silent for two independent reasons: throttled() is True (last_reminder 2026-08-23T14:13:49Z, inside the 20h window) and build_message() returns '' (AGF last commit 0d ago, AGR 4d ago, both 0 unpushed, against a 14d cadence). An end-to-end stdin run confirmed exit 0, no stdout, an activity record with decision='throttled', and the live state file byte-identical (md5) before and after. SEPARATE COVERAGE GAP for a human: the sibling test_repo_sync_cadence_trigger.py has three tests and all three mock.patch.object(rsc, 'throttled', return_value=True), so the existing suite never once executes build_message(). Its enforcement path is green-but-unexercised, which is the pattern this audit exists to catch, even though the path does work when called directly.
